text: The pretraining stage from lesson one needs an enormous, carefully built supply of data. This lesson walks that data pipeline end to end, from raw web crawl to the tensors a training loop actually consumes, so chapter two's deep dives all slot into one picture.

Text starts as raw crawl data, code, and books, and gets extracted and cleaned of boilerplate. It's then filtered by language and quality and deduplicated so the model doesn't over-memorize repeated content. From there it's tokenized into integer IDs and packed into fixed-length sequences. Finally, multiple domains get sampled at chosen rates and written out as training-ready shards. Each of those stages gets its own full lesson later in this chapter, but the order they run in matters just as much as what each one does on its own.

Hugging Face's datasets library, especially in streaming mode, is the standard tool for assembling a pipeline like this. Streaming matters because pretraining corpora run into terabytes, far larger than most local disks, so data is read, transformed, and discarded on the fly rather than loaded into memory all at once. The same streaming dataset object can be filtered, mapped, and chained through every later stage without ever touching the full corpus on disk.

Skipping any one stage has a real cost. No deduplication means wasted compute re-memorizing text, with a real risk of test-set contamination. No quality filtering means the model spends its capacity learning from spam. And no packing means GPU time burned processing padding tokens that carry no signal at all.

By the time training starts, every expensive decision about what data to include has already been made upstream. Next up, lesson four: the model architecture choices that decide what happens to those tokens.
